1	# DEVDESK-754 — `:sec` "Group by fix" (`g`): one row per cause, CVE first
2	
3	Story SC, estimated L. Measured here at **L + M**: split into **SC1 (CVE by package, AC1, AC3-AC7
4	for the CVE tab)** and **SC2 (Misconfig by file and fix, AC2)**, one PR each, SC1 first. Worktree
5	`.worktrees/feat/sec-group-by-fix-754`, cut from `0800ae5b`. **Rebase on `origin/main` once
6	DEVDESK-753 is merged, before step 3**: 753 edits the same spots (`findings.go` enter case,
7	`details.go` esc case, `model.go` fields, `view.go` status, `header.go` help, `scanning.md`).
8	The tester writes each step's tests first; the coder makes them pass.
9	
10	## Facts checked (2026-11-23)
11	
12	- `remediation.Group` (fixes.go:92) has **no production caller**; the header's `Fixable` comes from
13	  `remediation.Summarize`. Group is free to extend; Summarize must not change.
14	- Header at 80 columns: info column `(80-2)/4 = 19`, logo kept (78 >= 19+40), so the shortcut
15	  column is **19 cells** and shows only the first chunk of 7 entries
16	  (`app_header.go` `splitArrayIntoChunks(…, 7)`). Results today: 16 entries; visible at 80 are
17	  `tab, enter, space, ctrl+o, S, c, h`. At 120 the column is 49 cells: chunk 1 (27 cells) plus
18	  about 20 cells of chunk 2. At 175 (90 cells) all three chunks fit. `<g> Group by fix` is 16
19	  cells: it fits a chunk at any width, but it is **visible at 80 only in the first 7** (Q1).
20	- Tab bar: `" " + RenderTabs(6 tabs)`. Width with 1-digit counts = 78, with 2-digit counts = 84,
21	  with 3-digit counts = 89. `PadWithBg` does not clip and the router does not clip the footer.
22	  **The 6-tab bar already overflows 80 columns** as soon as counts have two digits (Q2). A 7th
23	  tab is impossible: confirmed.
24	- 753's detail uses `->` in its Change section (`libfoo 0.8.0 -> 0.17.0`): reuse `->`, not `→`.
25	- The detail of a finding is reached from one place today (`handleResultsState` enter, which 753
26	  extends with `startChangePreview`); esc in details hard-codes `StateResults`; `refreshDetails`
27	  falls back to `StateResults`.
28	
29	## Design (option A recommended)
30	
31	- **A (recommended): a toggle in `StateResults` + a new level `StateGroup`.** `grouped` is a display
32	  toggle of the results (lowercase `g`, Rule 111 local toggle): the body renders a second
33	  `datatable.Model[fixGroup]` instead of `findingsTable`; the findings table is not touched, so its
34	  filter, sort and cursor survive (AC4 for free). `enter` on a group opens `StateGroup`: a table of
35	  the group's findings (`findingColumns()`), `esc` back to the grouped list. `enter` there opens
36	  `StateDetails` with `detailsParent = StateGroup`; esc/refresh return to `detailsParent`.
37	- B: reuse `StateResults` with a "group" filter token on the findings table. Rejected: it rewrites
38	  the user's filter (AC4), the header count and tab semantics, and `esc` meaning.
39	- C: group detail as viewport text. Rejected: AC3 needs to open one finding (a selectable row).
40	
41	What a group row shows (all cells plain text, Rule 122; only Severity coloured, as in the findings
42	table, and the severity is also its word; Fix/Change/count in `ColorText`, no colour as sole carrier):
43	
44	| Tab | Columns (Sizing) |
45	|---|---|
46	| CVE | Severity (Fixed 10) · Package (Content, min 14) · Change (Content, min 16, Flex 1) `1.1.1k -> 1.1.1w`, `1.2 -> 1.3 or 2.0` (ambiguous), `1.2 -> none` · CVEs (Fixed 5) · Fix (Content, min 16, max 24, Optional) |
47	| Misconfig (SC2) | Severity · File (Content, TruncateHead, max 40) · Rule (Content, ID) · Findings (Fixed 8) · Fix (Content, min 16, max 24, Optional) |
48	
49	Fix column = the 751 closed vocabulary through `fixStatusOf(member, onDisk)` (never the 753
50	preview, which exists for one finding only). CVE: fixable -> `Manual` (751 mapping), unfixed ->
51	`No fix published`. 80 columns: CVE 12+16+18+7+18 = 71 <= 78, Misconfig 12+18+16+10+18 = 74.
52	
53	Which groups are listed: groups are built from **all** findings of the tab (so the count and the
54	target are what one move closes), and a group is shown when **at least one member is in
55	`findingsTable.Visible()`** (severity tokens, search, Pod Security filter apply). Order: worst
56	severity, then member count descending, then subject, then change (deterministic).
57	
58	## Steps — SC1 (one PR)
59	
60	1. **Pure grouping of vulnerabilities** (`internal/remediation/fixes.go`, `fixes_test.go`).
61	   Add `Fix.Unfixed bool`, `Fix.Members []scan.Finding`, `func (f Fix) Key() FixKey`
62	   (`FixKey{Ecosystem, Package, Installed string; Unfixed bool}`, exported) and
63	   `func GroupAll(findings []scan.Finding) []Fix`: Group's fixable fixes, plus one unfixed Fix per
64	   (ecosystem, package, installed) with no FixedIn, plus one Fix per vulnerability with no PkgName
65	   (Package = its ID). `Group` keeps its contract (fixable only) and fills `Members`.
66	   Tests: 3 CVEs of one package with 1.2/1.3/1.4 -> one Fix, Target 1.4, 3 CVEs, Command set;
67	   same package, 2 installed versions -> 2 fixes; 1 fixed + 1 unfixed CVE of one package -> 2 rows,
68	   one `Unfixed`; ambiguous FixedIn -> Target "" and Options listed; no PkgName -> one row each;
69	   non-vulnerabilities ignored; order (severity, count, package); **invariant** sum of
70	   `len(CVEs)` over `!Unfixed` == `Summarize(f).Fixable()` (AC5), table-driven + a fuzz seed.
71	   Done when `go test ./internal/remediation` passes. Parallel with step 2.
72	2. **UI group model, pure** (new `internal/ui/security/fixgroup.go`, `fixgroup_test.go`).
73	   `type fixGroup struct{ Key groupKey; Severity scan.SeverityLevel; Subject, Change string; Status fixStatus; Command string; Members []scan.Finding }`;
74	   `func cveGroups(findings []scan.Finding) []fixGroup` (from `remediation.GroupAll`; Change uses
75	   `->`; Command = `Fix.Command`, "" when not `scan.PlainWords`);
76	   `func visibleGroups(all []fixGroup, visible []scan.Finding) []fixGroup` (member match by `sameFinding`);
77	   `func groupIndexOf(groups []fixGroup, f scan.Finding) int` (-1 if none);
78	   `func groupIndexByKey(groups []fixGroup, key groupKey, prev int) int` (key, else clamp(prev));
79	   `func nearestFinding(visible []scan.Finding, g *fixGroup, prev *scan.Finding, prevCursor int) int`
80	   (first visible member of g; else prev if still visible; else clamp(prevCursor); -1 if empty).
81	   Tests: each function's table, incl. empty inputs, filter hiding every member, a group gone after
82	   a re-scan, a key collision across two installed versions. Done: `go test ./internal/ui/security -run Group`.
83	3. **Toggle `g` and the grouped table** (depends on 1, 2; after the 753 rebase). `model.go`:
84	   `grouped bool`, `groups datatable.Model[fixGroup]`; `findings.go`: `groupKey = "g"`,
85	   `canGroup() shortcut.Availability` (`reasonGroupNotHere = "Group by fix covers the CVE tab"`,
86	   SC2 widens it to "the CVE and Misconfig tabs"; `reasonNothingToGroup`), `toggleGroup()`
87	   (on: build, cursor on `groupIndexOf(selected finding)`; off: `findingsTable.SetCursor(nearestFinding(…))`,
88	   never `updateFindingsTable`/`GotoTop`), `refreshGroups()` called after every findings-table
89	   change (token, search key, `p`, `setResult`); in grouped mode `.` sorts the groups table, `/`
90	   and `c h m l p` still drive the findings table; `ctrl+o`, `space`, `S` greyed with a reason
91	   (`reasonOpenTheGroup = "Open the group to act on one finding"`). `switchTab` keeps `grouped`
92	   (Q3). `view.go`: body = `m.groups.View()` when grouped; footer Status in grouped mode is the
93	   selected group, e.g. `3 CVEs closed by one move to 1.1.1w` / `No fix published for 2 CVEs`
94	   (truncated by `FooterMessage`). `header.go`: `{Key: "g", Description: "Group by fix"}` (label
95	   `List by finding` when on) in `resultsShortcuts`, at the position Q1 decides; help KeyBinding +
96	   a "Group by fix" section. `internal/ui/keymap/keymap.go`: add `g` to `security/findings` + a
97	   test like `pss_filter_test.go`. Tests: AC1 (rows, delta, count), AC4 (`g g` keeps tokens,
98	   `SortState`, query; selection = first visible member of the group under the cursor), AC6
99	   (`RenderedWidth() == width-2` at 80/120/175 for both tables, `ansi.Strip(cell) == cell`, the
100	   header's shortcut lines `<= col2Width`, `g` in `GetHelpContent`, same key set grouped or not on
101	   every tab, `g` greyed + footer Warn on Secrets/Licenses/CI/Remediation, and on Misconfig until
102	   SC2). Done: package tests + `TestEveryLowercaseBindingIsDeclared` green.
103	4. **Group level and the detail's parent** (depends on 3). `model.go`: `StateGroup`,
104	   `openGroup *groupKey`, `groupTable datatable.Model[scan.Finding]`, `detailsParent ViewState`.
105	   Extract `openDetail(f scan.Finding, parent ViewState) (Model, tea.Cmd)` from the enter case
106	   (keeps 753's `startChangePreview`). `details.go` esc -> `m.state = m.detailsParent` (and 753's
107	   preview reset). `refreshDetails` falls back to `detailsParent`, or to `StateResults` when the
108	   group is gone. `StateGroup` keys: `esc Back`, `enter Details`, `Y Copy cmd` (group command,
109	   greyed `reasonNoGroupCommand`), `? Help`; title `… › <subject> <change>`; header count/Fixable/
110	   unrendered/PSS/signature conditions include `StateGroup`; `InEditMode` false; `handlePaste`
111	   drops. Tests: AC3 path results(g) -> enter -> group -> enter -> detail -> esc -> group -> esc ->
112	   grouped list on the same group; 751 keys from that detail (enter, ctrl+o, Y, X greyed/enabled as
113	   on the flat path); 753 preview starts on open; `Y` in group copies `go get …` whole.
114	5. **Re-scan truth (AC5, AC7)** (depends on 4). `setResult` -> `refreshGroups` (cursor by key),
115	   then refresh `StateGroup` (members by key; group gone -> grouped list), then `refreshDetails`.
116	   Groups are derived, never stored as "done". Tests: verification re-scan removes one CVE of a
117	   3-CVE group -> row shows 2; removes all -> row gone, cursor nearest; reopening a result keeps
118	   `grouped` (Q3); no "done" field exists (grep test not needed, review).
119	6. **Docs** (with step 5): `docs/architecture/scanning.md` (grouping, `GroupAll`, the invariant,
120	   the levels), `.claude/rules/tui-layout.md` Rule 111 security toggles `c h m l p g`,
121	   `docs-site/docs/how-to/run-a-security-scan.md` (techwriter).
122	
123	## Steps — SC2 (second PR, after SC1 merged)
124	
125	7. `misconfigGroups(findings []scan.Finding, onDisk bool) []fixGroup`: key (File,
126	   `remediation.RuleKey(ID)`, `fixState`); Status label shared, `Built-in fix unavailable` without
127	   reason when members' reasons differ; Command = the members' single plain `runCommand`, else "".
128	   Tests: 3 instances of one rule in one file -> 1 row of 3; same rule in 2 files -> 2 rows; one
129	   declined + one available -> 2 rows; image target -> `Cannot fix here`; no catalog rule -> `Manual`
130	   / `No guidance available`; nothing counted in `Fixable`.
131	8. Misconfig columns (File visible), `canGroup` enabled on Misconfig, the `p` filter applies,
132	   ctrl+o from a detail opened in a group -> verification -> group refreshed. Help + docs.
133	
134	## Risks, traps
135	
136	- Conflict with 753 (rebase first). `updateFindingsTable` calls `GotoTop`: never call it on toggle.
137	- `sameFinding` ignores the line: two instances with equal Title+Message in one file are one
138	  identity; nearest-selection may land on the first of them (acceptable, documented).
139	- The group's Fix label comes from `fixStatusOf`, the detail's from 753's `m.fixStatus` (adds the
140	  stale preview): a group may say `Built-in fix available` while its detail says unavailable.
141	- `g` means find/go-to in viewer, workspaces and explorer; here a group toggle (Rule 101, accepted
142	  by the story; declared local toggle).
143	- Irreversible: nothing (no cache or config format change). `Fix` gains fields; no caller outside tests.
144	
145	## Questions
146	
147	- **Q1 (product)** Position of `g` in the results column: (a) 3rd, after `enter` — visible at 80,
148	  pushes `h Toggle HIGH` out of the first chunk (recommended: the story's key feature should be
149	  visible at 80); (b) after `l` — visible from about 120 only.
150	- **Q2 (scope)** AC6 "every line within the width at 80": the 6-tab row already reaches 84 cells
151	  with 2-digit counts. (a) Out of scope, separate bug, AC6 tested on header, table and footer info
152	  line (recommended); (b) fix it here (compact labels or clip), +S.
153	- **Q3 (product)** Lifetime of `grouped`: (a) held for the view's life per tab, survives tab switch
154	  and reopening a result, so a re-scan then reopen lands on the grouped list (recommended); (b) one
155	  visit of the tab, like the Pod Security filter. Neither adds auto-reload of a result when a scan
156	  of the target on screen finishes elsewhere (today's behavior, unchanged; it would be +M).
157	- **Q4 (product)** Misconfig count: AC2 says "findings closed"; a built-in fix acts on one finding
158	  per `ctrl+o`. Column titled `Findings` (count), no "closed" claim (recommended), or "Closes".

16	// ViewState represents the current state of the security view.
17	//
18	// There were five. StateInput was the form, and StateScanning the screen that
19	// ran one scan in place while the user watched it — both went with the form
20	// (phase 3). What replaced them is the inventory, which rescans in the
21	// background with a spinner on the row, so nothing waits on a whole screen.
22	type ViewState int
23	
24	const (
25		StateInventory ViewState = iota // What this context has scanned, read from the caches
26		StateResults                    // Displaying results summary
27		StateDetails                    // Showing detailed findings
28		StateGroup                      // The findings of one group of the grouped list (DEVDESK-754)
29	)
30	
31	// Model represents the security scanner view
32	type Model struct {
33		config *config.Config
34		// secrets is the context's store, used only to load the forge token for a
35		// CI scan. Nothing else here reads a credential.
36		secrets credentials.Storage
37		width   int
38		height  int
39	
40		state  ViewState
41		result *scan.Result
42	
43		// deps is the router's detection of the scanners, nil until it lands.
44		deps *scan.Report
45	
46		// Inventory state
47		inventory datatable.Model[scanTarget]
48	
49		// jobs is the router snapshot of everything running anywhere. See jobs.go:
50		// the rows' activity is derived from it, so there is no in-flight state here
51		// to carry across a reload.
52		jobs []jobs.Run
53	
54		// failures is a copy of the registry's remembered failures, replaced (never
55		// merged) by handleJobsChanged, and contextName the context the snapshot was
56		// built for (ChangedMsg.Context).
57		failures    []jobs.Failure
58		contextName string
59	
60		// inventoryLoading is true while loadInventoryCmd is in flight. It exists
61		// because an empty table and a table that has not answered yet look the
62		// same, and they mean opposite things: "Nothing scanned yet" asserted
63		// before the caches were read is a claim the view cannot make, and the one
64		// the user saw flash by before the list appeared.
65		//
66		// It also drives the shared activity dot (status, WantsBlink).
67		inventoryLoading bool
68	
69		// targetPath is what the result on screen is about — an image reference or a
70		// repository path. It is the directory .gitleaksignore is written into, so
71		// it is the key and never a display form.
72		targetPath string
73		// targetLabel is the same target folded for the title: the registry prefix
74		// replaced by its alias, or the home directory by "~". It is a second field
75		// rather than a folding applied to targetPath because the two are read for
76		// opposite purposes — one is shown, the other is written to disk, and an
77		// aliased path names a directory that does not exist.
78		targetLabel string
79	
80		// Results state
81		findingsTable datatable.Model[scan.Finding]
82		// selectedFinding is what the details view is showing. It holds the finding
83		// rather than its row index, so a list that changes underneath cannot make
84		// the details describe a different one.
85		selectedFinding *scan.Finding
86		activeTab       int // 0=CVE, 1=Secrets, 2=Licenses, 3=Misconfig, 4=CI, 5=Remediation
87	
88		// remediation is the Remediation tab: base images and the tags they could
89		// move to. It is read for the result on screen and reset with it.
90		remediation remediationState
91	
92		// misconfigPending is the file a confirmed misconfiguration fix would
93		// write, held between the confirmation and the write (§3.78). It carries
94		// the bytes the diff was computed from, so what gets written is what was
95		// agreed to and not a second reading of the file.
96		misconfigPending *preparedWrite
97		// misconfigFinding is the finding that pending write is about, kept so the
98		// verification re-scan knows what to look for.
99		misconfigFinding misconfigFindingRef
100	
101		// misconfigVerifying is the fix waiting on the re-scan that decides whether
102		// it worked (§3.78, phase B3). A written file is not a fixed one: the rule
103		// is judged by a measurement, never by the catalog's own confidence.
104		misconfigVerifying *misconfigVerify
105	
106		// changePreview is the stored answer to "what would the built-in fix change in
107		// the finding on screen" (DEVDESK-753), written by Update only. previewSeq
108		// numbers the requests so a late answer is told from the current one.
109		changePreview changePreview
110		previewSeq    int
111	
112		// SKELETON (DEVDESK-754, steps 3 to 5): the fields of "Group by fix". The
113		// real wiring replaces every line of this block.
114		//
115		// groupedTabs is the display mode, held per tab for the life of the view.
116		groupedTabs [tabCount]bool
117		// groups is the grouped list that replaces the findings table's body.
118		groups datatable.Model[fixGroup]
119		// openGroup is the group StateGroup shows, by key; nil outside it.
120		openGroup *groupKey
121		// groupTable lists the findings of openGroup, with the findings' columns.
122		groupTable datatable.Model[scan.Finding]
123		// detailsParent is the level esc returns to from the detail.
124		detailsParent ViewState
125	
126		// OriginView is the view to return to when Esc is pressed in StateResults.
127		// Set by the app router when opening this view from workspaces or
128		// oci_resources. Empty when the results were opened from the inventory,
129		// which is inside this view and needs no round trip.
130		OriginView command.ViewType
131	
132		// footer is the one line of transient state below the viewport (Rule 128).
133		footer sharedcomponents.FooterMessage
134	
135		// Details view scrollable viewport
136		detailsViewport viewport.Model
137	
138		// Ignore secret confirmation
139		confirmModal    *sharedcomponents.ConfirmModal
140		findingToIgnore *scan.Finding
141	
142		// scanAllModal carries the purge checkbox for A. It is separate from
143		// confirmModal because the two answer different messages, and one field
144		// holding either would make the handler guess which question was asked.
145		scanAllModal *sharedcomponents.OptionConfirmModal
146	}
147	
148	// New creates a new security scanner view, on the inventory.
149	// New builds the view. The secret store comes in at construction, like
150	// workspaces': the CI stage needs the context's forge token, and a rescan
151	// started here must produce the same grade as the same rescan started from ws —
152	// two screens grading one repository differently is the shape §3.11 and §3.12
153	// each had to undo.
154	func New(cfg *config.Config, secrets credentials.Storage) Model {
155		t := datatable.New(datatable.Config[scan.Finding]{
156			Columns:        findingColumns(),
157			SortColumn:     -1, // the order the scanner reported
158			SelectedStyles: findingSelectedStyles,
159			Tokens:         findingTokens(),
160			TokenMatch:     matchesFinding(cfg.Scan.EffectivePSSProfile()),
161		})
162	
163		return Model{
164			config:    cfg,
165			secrets:   secrets,
166			state:     StateInventory,
167			inventory: newInventoryTable(cfg.Scan.Categories.CI.Enabled, cfg.Scan.Categories.Misconfig.Enabled),
168			// True from construction, because Init loads unconditionally: a view
169			// that starts saying "not loading" would render the empty message for
170			// the frame before the first Cmd runs.
171			inventoryLoading: true,
172			findingsTable:    t,
173			remediation:      newRemediationState(),
174			// SKELETON (DEVDESK-754): built here so the zero value of a table is
175			// never read.
176			groups:     newGroupsTable(),
177			groupTable: newGroupFindingsTable(cfg),
178		}
179	}
180	
181	// ciForgeURL is the forge a repository must belong to for the CI column to be
182	// able to grade it — and the empty string when the column is off, which is what
183	// spares the loader a git call per row.
184	func ciForgeURL(cfg *config.Config) string {
185		if cfg == nil || !cfg.Scan.Categories.CI.Enabled {
186			return ""
187		}
188		return cfg.Forge.URL
189	}
190	
191	func (m Model) ciForgeURL() string { return ciForgeURL(m.config) }
192	
193	// severityTokens are the four cumulative severity filters (Rule 136).
194	//
195	// They replaced a cycle on `.` — which also cost the table its sort key. A
196	// cycle can only ask "at least this severe", and the question actually asked is
197	// "CRITICAL and HIGH", which is not a threshold: it excludes MEDIUM while
198	// including CRITICAL. Four toggles can say it and a cycle never could.
199	func severityTokens() []sharedcomponents.FilterToken {
200		return []sharedcomponents.FilterToken{
201			{Label: "critical"}, {Label: "high"}, {Label: "medium"}, {Label: "low"},
202		}
203	}
204	
205	// severityToken maps a finding's severity onto its token label. UNKNOWN has no
206	// token, so it is only ever hidden by an explicit choice of others.
207	var severityToken = REDACTED
208		scan.SeverityCritical: "critical",
209		scan.SeverityHigh:     "high",
210		scan.SeverityMedium:   "medium",
211		scan.SeverityLow:      "low",
212	}
213	
214	// matchesSeverity keeps everything while no severity token is active: an empty
215	// filter means "no opinion", not "nothing". It reads the four severity tokens
216	// only, so the Pod Security token alone does not count as a severity choice.
217	func matchesSeverity(f scan.Finding, active map[string]bool) bool {
218		chosen := false
219		for _, label := range severityToken {
220			chosen = chosen || active[label]
221		}
222		if !chosen {
223			return true
224		}
225		return active[severityToken[f.Severity]]
226	}
227	
228	// NewWithPreloadedResult creates a security view showing a stored scan result.
229	// Used to display cached results without re-scanning (Rule 126).
230	func NewWithPreloadedResult(cfg *config.Config, secrets credentials.Storage, result *scan.Result) Model {
231		m := New(cfg, secrets)
232		m.state = StateResults
233		m.result = result
234		m.targetPath = result.Target
235		m.targetLabel = labelForResult(cfg, result)
236		m.activeTab = TabCVE
237		// Filled here rather than waiting for the first WindowSizeMsg: the rows do
238		// not depend on the width any more, so nothing was gained by deferring and
239		// the table was empty until the terminal happened to report its size.
240		m.updateFindingsTable()
241		return m
242	}
243	
244	// setResult puts a freshly measured result on screen, keeping the tab and the
245	// filters the user is looking through. It is what a verification re-scan hands
246	// back, so the table stops listing a rule the edit has already dealt with.
247	func (m *Model) setResult(result *scan.Result) {
248		m.result = result
249		m.targetPath = result.Target
250		m.targetLabel = labelForResult(m.config, result)
251		m.updateFindingsTable()
252		// The file the preview was about has just been rewritten: forget it, the
253		// verdict asks again (restartChangePreview).
254		m.changePreview = changePreview{}
255		// A detail open on the finding the edit dealt with must follow the new
256		// reading, or close with the reason the verdict puts in the footer.
257		m.refreshDetails()
258	}
259	
260	// Init initializes the model
261	func (m Model) Init() tea.Cmd {
262		// Loaded whatever the opening state: a view opened on a result returns
263		// to the inventory on ctrl+r, and reading two small files is cheaper
264		// than the branch that would decide not to.
265		return loadInventoryCmd(m.ciForgeURL())
266	}
267	
268	// InEditMode reports whether a field or a modal has the keyboard, which is what
269	// stops the router claiming ":", "q" and "?" for itself.
270	//
271	// The results and details states used to be listed here too, for one reason: it
272	// was the only way to be handed esc. The router forwards esc unconditionally now
273	// (§1.3 D15), so those states are ordinary again — and get the command line, the
274	// help overlay and quit back with them.
275	func (m Model) InEditMode() bool {
276		switch {
277		case m.confirmModal != nil, m.scanAllModal != nil:
278			return true
279		case m.state == StateInventory:
280			return m.inventory.InEditMode()
281		case m.state == StateResults:
282			// The findings table gained a filter bar with the severity tokens, so
283			// this state has a focused field to declare like any other.
284			return m.findingsTable.InEditMode()
285		}
286		return false
287	}

# entire-graph — instructions for coding agents (follow directly)

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,
types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

## Hard rules

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.
2. READ focused source around the result. Widen the check when aliases, generated code, dynamic
   dispatch, or related implementations could matter.
3. Use graph follow-ups only when they answer a real question. For impact or callers, prefer:
       entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X
4. Make the smallest complete edit and check sibling sites or contracts when the task implies them.
5. VERIFY before stopping. Run the most focused relevant test, build, or reproduction available.
   If execution is unavailable, perform a bounded source-level verification and state the limit.
6. Prefer precise queries and line ranges, but never trade resolution for fewer turns.
7. Feature-detect before relying on semantic relations:
       entire graph capabilities --json

## When NOT to use the graph

If the task already names the exact file and it is small, just read it — the graph saves tokens
by eliminating exploration; when there is nothing to explore, skip it.

## Reference

    locate  ->  entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "..."
    impact  ->  entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X   (one shot: callers, callees, type consumers, data flow, co-change, siblings)

    detect  ->  entire graph capabilities --json   (inventory-only languages have no relations)
    stats   ->  entire graph stats --repo .        (human-facing token-savings report; not part of your workflow — do not run it unless asked)

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all
>   in scope. Planning is no longer delegated to Gemini (Antigravity).
> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`. Open work (stories, tasks, bugs) is tracked
>   in Plane, see the `## Plane` section of the root `CLAUDE.md`.
> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP; a Proxy row says whether a proxy variable applies, the checks themselves stay direct, DEVDESK-582) + real-time port monitoring (`K` stops a process: SIGTERM, up to 5 s, then a confirmed SIGKILL on Linux and macOS, at once on Windows; DevDesk itself, its direct parent, PID 1 and Windows PIDs 0 and 4 are refused; the identity is checked at each signal, DEVDESK-711) + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only) + a path trace under Diagnostics (Trace Path button, or `H` on the route row; no separate tab since DEVDESK-471) (native path trace, on native Linux, native Windows (IPv4 only, ICMP echoes through `iphlpapi`, DEVDESK-486) and WSL2: on macOS and WSL1 the button, `H`, `enter` and `ctrl+o` are greyed and the footer says why, DEVDESK-334; the column starts with this machine, its interface and its gateway; `ctrl+o` can start it from a running Docker Engine container instead (container and network rows, hops still traced from this machine); `H` on the Diagnostics route row opens the trace level on that host without starting it (greyed with the reason on an unsupported platform or a target the trace refuses; its interface and gateway rows reuse the Local route check's reading of the same address, read once, DEVDESK-473), and in the trace level `enter` starts or restarts it, `ctrl+o` picks the source, `esc` cancels then goes back where it came from; under WSL2 the source row says `WSL2 (VM), not the Windows host` with the networking mode, and in NAT mode the gateway and TTL 1 hop are tagged `Windows host (virtual switch)` only when proven, DEVDESK-333; the interface row says `no route` when the kernel proves there is none and `undetermined` when the routing table could not be read, a no-route error keeps the local rows, a trace that ends on the hop limit or the deadline folds its silent tail into one `silent` row and marks the `last to answer` hop, and the target refuses a `:port`, DEVDESK-335)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, when its transcript is gone, or while the terminal is not focused (header `Updates › paused`, then `paused (terminal not focused)`; `app.when_unfocused: run` keeps it live); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go
mise run ci           # the five checks in order (fmt-check, vet, lint, build, test-race), stops at the first failure; unlike check it rewrites no file and also runs build and test-race. `test-race` is the only test run (`-race` covers `go test`); `mise run test` stays available alone for the fast local loop. CI runs fmt-check, vet, lint and build in the `Lint and build` job and `test-race` in the `Test` job, on every pull request, docs-only ones included (the docs-only shortcut applies to `Lint and build` only); the whole CI targets under 10 minutes, so run this locally before a PR to catch a red check early

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when no configured helper is `store` (plaintext) or `cache` (memory with a timeout), by name, path or shell command: `approve` reaches every helper. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one. Every host store operation (the probe, `Save`, `Load`,
`Delete`) is bounded to 3 s: a store that does not answer, such as a locked
Secret Service waiting on an unlock prompt over SSH, is skipped like an absent
one, `Detail` says so, and it is not asked again while that call is stuck
(`internal/credentials/hoststore_bound.go`, DEVDESK-745).

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view. It takes the `Selection` and moves nothing when it does not
persist (memory), and removes a secret from the YAML only once it reads back
from the store; otherwise it stays and the note says so (DEVDESK-745).

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Nexus tests replay recorded fixtures (DEVDESK-511, DEVDESK-580).** Three campaigns
in `internal/nexusfixture/fixtures/` (`catalog`, `cachedonly`, `access`) replay through
`fakenexus`: `mise run test` needs no bench, cluster or secret. A `record: pending` file is never
versioned (`TestNoPendingFixtureIsVersioned`); `DEVDESK_FIXTURE_RECORDING=1` only in a local recording session.
`nexus-bench record` without `--state` applies no state filter and can overwrite an `upstream-cut` fixture.
Bench writes go only through `nexus-bench:*` tasks and the guarded `DEVDESK_NEXUS_BENCH_SCENARIOS=1` test.
Dated measures live in `docs/measurements/`; a measure contradicting a criterion or the code is frozen and noted, never fixed in the same PR.

**Scanner containers and the proxy (DEVDESK-583, D164).** Every `run --rm` a scanner
issues goes through `containerRun{…}.cmd()` (`internal/scan/container_run.go`): the proxy
variables travel as `-e NAME` with the value in the child environment, never in argv. The
guard `TestContainerGuard*` (`internal/netproxy/container_guard_test.go`) fails on any other
`"run"` literal; only the two permanent exceptions in that file are allowed. The tests of
`internal/scan`, `internal/app` and `internal/ui/security` neutralise the seams
`proxyForward` / `containerForward` in their `TestMain`, so a developer's `HTTPS_PROXY` does not
change an exact argv. The `TestMain` of `internal/app`
also replaces `detectTools` (`internal/app/scan_tools.go`, production value `scan.Detect`) with an
empty report, so `App.Init` never runs the `trivy`, `gitleaks` and `plumber` of the machine
(DEVDESK-645); `TestInitDoesNotRunTheScannersOfTheHost` and `TestDetectToolsIsScanDetectInProduction`
guard it.

**Tests and the host secret store (DEVDESK-610).** By default `credentials.Select` and
`KeyringAvailable` reach the real keyring of the machine (Secret Service over D-Bus on
Linux); a locked keyring blocks the whole suite until the timeout. A test binary that can
reach them isolates the store: `fakekeyring.Install()` in `TestMain`, then
`fakekeyring.Fresh(t)` (or `FreshUnreachable(t, err)` for a locked keyring) per test, from
`internal/testutil/fakekeyring`. `isolateHome(t)` already calls `Fresh` in `internal/app` and
`internal/ui/setup`. Two guards enforce it: at run time, any keyring or `git credential` call
in a test binary without the fake panics with `DEVDESK-610` and the operation; statically,
`TestHostStoreGuard*` (`internal/credentials/hoststore_guard_test.go`) fails on K1 (go-keyring
imported outside `internal/credentials`), K2 (`SwapHostStoreForTest` in non-test code) and K3
(`fakekeyring` imported by non-test code). The seam is `credentials.HostStore` and
`SwapHostStoreForTest`, reserved for tests (it panics outside a test binary). Limits: the
runtime guard only sees the paths a test runs; the static one misses an aliased package
name, a dynamic import and an external binary; `gitHelperUsable` reads the git config
unguarded; `Install` and `Fresh` are global, so no `t.Parallel`. See
`docs/architecture/configuration.md`, "Testing code that reaches the secret store".

**Tests and real signals (DEVDESK-708, DEVDESK-711).** A test must never signal a real process. In
`internal/ports` the only place that does is `realOS.kill(pid, want, sig)` (`internal/ports/procos.go`),
reached through the `procOS` seam, which also holds `identity` and `probe` (`Probe` reads the state, it
sends no signal). `selfPID`, `parentPID`, `goos` and `now` are seams too. A test substitutes them
(`useFakeOS(t, self, parent, goos)` in `seams_test.go`); in `internal/ui/netdiag` it replaces `processOps`
on the model, so `ports.Kill`, `ports.Terminate` and `ports.Probe` are never reached.
`IdentityForTest` and `DeferredIdentityForTest` panic outside a test binary.
Two guards enforce it: at run time, a real signal in a test binary panics with `DEVDESK-708`
unless the test called `allowRealSignals(t)`, which only a test that kills a child it
started itself may do (`TestKillEndsARealChildProcess`, `TestTerminateEndsARealChildProcess` in
`stop_real_test.go`); statically, `TestOnlyRealOSSendsASignal`
fails on a signalling call (`os.FindProcess`, `syscall.Kill`, `unix.Kill`,
`windows.TerminateProcess`, `.Kill(` or `.Signal(`) outside `(realOS) kill`. Limits: the static
guard misses an aliased import, another package and an external binary; the seams are global, so
no `t.Parallel`. See `docs/architecture/network.md`, "Seams and the signal guard".

**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
literal `tea.KeyPressMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` returns a
`tea.KeyPressMsg` (`Keys` and `Type` return a message list), `Paste` a `tea.PasteMsg`; `Key` is strict: an unknown name
panics. The space key is built as a key (`Key("space")`), never matched through
`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). Lip Gloss v2 has no global colour profile (`Style.Render` always emits full
colour), so a test needs no setup to check styling; it reads the SGR or strips it
with `ansi.Strip`. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a
hand-built key, a `colorprofile` import outside `internal/app/profile_test.go` and
`internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go` or `SetColorProfile` in any `_test.go`. Paste tests
(`internal/app/paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input_test.go`, `component_form_test.go`):
a paste reaches the focused field, newlines become spaces in single-line fields,
and no key action fires (Rule 111).

**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as
`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Update
handlers switch on `tea.KeyPressMsg`, never the `tea.KeyMsg` interface (it also
matches releases). A paste is a `tea.PasteMsg`, not a key (Rule 111). Guards in
`internal/ui/keymap` (`space_scan_test.go`, `legacy_key_scan_test.go`,
`viewport_keymap_scan_test.go`) fail the suite otherwise; limits are listed in
`docs/architecture/app-shell.md`.

## Dependencies

Go 1.27 (`go 1.27.3` in `go.mod`). Key libraries (versions as in `go.mod`):
- `charm.land/bubbletea/v2` (v2.1.1) - TUI framework (v2: `tea.KeyPressMsg`, `tea.PasteMsg`, `View() tea.View`)
- `charm.land/bubbles/v2` (v2.2.1) - Pre-built TUI components (table, textinput, viewport)
- `charm.land/lipgloss/v2` (v2.0.6) - Styling (no global colour profile; colours are `image/color.Color`)
- `github.com/charmbracelet/colorprofile` (v0.4.3) - colour profile `main.go` forces under Windows Terminal (replaces `termenv`)
- `github.com/NimbleMarkets/ntcharts/v2` (v2.9.0) - dashboard sparkline
- `github.com/charmbracelet/x/ansi` - ANSI-safe width, strip and cut
- `gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go` - GitLab API client
- `github.com/prometheus-community/pro-bing` - ICMP ping functionality (maintained fork of go-ping/ping)
- `github.com/google/go-github/v68` - GitHub API client (§3.6)
- `github.com/libp2p/go-netroute` - which interface a destination leaves by, on all three platforms (§3.44)
- `golang.org/x/sys` - direct (Rule 303): the socket calls of `internal/nettrace` (`IP_TTL`, `IP_RECVERR`, `recvmsg` on the error queue); `x/sys/windows` serves `iphlpapi` (the Windows path trace, `IcmpSendEcho2`)
- `github.com/zalando/go-keyring` - host secret manager (wincred / Keychain / Secret Service), no cgo
- `gopkg.in/yaml.v3` - YAML configuration

## Code Conventions

- Comments: **English only** (Rule 307) — existing French comments are not rewritten wholesale, but any new or edited comment is in English
- Commit messages: **English only** (Rule 307)
- UI text and logs: **English US only** (Rule 129)
- Bubbletea models define their own message types
- Use `theme` package for consistent styling (`internal/ui/theme/`)
- Config changes must call `config.Save()` to persist
- All colors defined in `theme/colors.go`, all styles in `theme/styles.go`
- Message naming: `[ComponentName][Action]Msg` (e.g., `ComponentFormSubmitMsg`)
- Context names: the rule exists twice (`config.ValidateContextName`, `contextcmd.ValidName`); change both or neither (`TestContextNameRulesAgree`). Creation refuses `-`, `new`, `list` (`config.ValidateNewContextName`); loading does not (D91)

## Critical Bubble Tea Rules

**NEVER modify model state inside a Cmd** (Rule 110) - Race condition:
- `Update()` is the ONLY place to modify model state
- `View()` is read-only
- `Cmd` functions do I/O and return messages

**NEVER use `style.Render()` inside `table.Row{}`** (Rule 122) - ANSI sequences corrupt all subsequent rows:
- Use plain text: `theme.IconError + " error"` not `theme.StatusErrorStyle.Render(...)`
- Apply row styling via `table.SetStyles(theme.TableStylesForState("error"))`

**Views render through `Render()`** (Bubble Tea v2): a top-level view implements
`Render() string` and `View() tea.View { return tea.NewView(m.Render()) }`; only the
router (`App.View()`) sets terminal state such as `AltScreen` and `BackgroundColor`. Components keep
`View() string`. Colours are `color.Color`; hex literals stay in `theme/colors.go`.

**Update() case extraction**: If a case block exceeds 5 lines, extract to `handle[MessageType]()` method returning `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP; a Proxy row says whether a proxy variable applies, the checks themselves stay direct, DEVDESK-582) + real-time port monitoring (`K` stops a process: SIGTERM, up to 5 s, then a confirmed SIGKILL on Linux and macOS, at once on Windows; DevDesk itself, its direct parent, PID 1 and Windows PIDs 0 and 4 are refused; the identity is checked at each signal, DEVDESK-711) + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only) + a path trace under Diagnostics (Trace Path button, or `H` on the route row; ## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go
mise run ci           # the five checks in order (fmt-check, vet, lint, build, test-race), stops at the first failure; unlike check it rewrites no file and also runs build and test-race. `test-race` is the only test run (`-race` covers `go test`); `mise run test` stays available alone for the fast local loop. CI runs fmt-check, vet, lint and build in the `Lint and build` job and `test-race` in the `Test` job, on every pull request, docs-only ones included (the docs-only shortcut applies to `Lint and build` only); the whole CI targets under 10 minutes, so run this locally before a PR to catch a red check early

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when no configured helper is `store` (plaintext) or `cache` (memory with a timeout), by name, path or shell command: `approve` reaches every helper. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one. Every host store operation (the probe, `Save`, `Load`,
`Delete`) is bounded to 3 s: a store that does not answer, such as a locked
Secret Service waiting on an unlock prompt over SSH, is skipped like an absent
one, `Detail` says so, and it is not asked again while that call is stuck
(`internal/credentials/hoststore_bound.go`, DEVDESK-745).

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view. It takes the `Selection` and moves nothing when it does not
persist (memory), and removes a secret from the YAML only once it reads back
from the store; otherwise it stays and the note says so (DEVDESK-745).

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Nexus tests replay recorded fixtures (DEVDESK-511, DEVDESK-580).** Three campaigns
in `internal/nexusfixture/fixtures/` (`catalog`, `cachedonly`, `access`) replay through
`fakenexus`: `mise run test` needs no bench, cluster or secret. A `record: pending` file is never
versioned (`TestNoPendingFixtureIsVersioned`); `DEVDESK_FIXTURE_RECORDING=1` only in a local recording session.
`nexus-bench record` without `--state` applies no state filter and can overwrite an `upstream-cut` fixture.
Bench writes go only through `nexus-bench:*` tasks and the guarded `DEVDESK_NEXUS_BENCH_SCENARIOS=1` test.
Dated measures live in `docs/measurements/`; a measure contradicting a criterion or the code is frozen and noted, never fixed in the same PR.

**Scanner containers and the proxy (DEVDESK-583, D164).** Every `run --rm` a scanner
issues goes through `containerRun{…}.cmd()` (`internal/scan/container_run.go`): the proxy
variables travel as `-e NAME` with the value in the child environment, never in argv. The
guard `TestContainerGuard*` (`internal/netproxy/container_guard_test.go`) fails on any other
`"run"` literal; only the two permanent exceptions in that file are allowed. The tests of
`internal/scan`, `internal/app` and `internal/ui/security` neutralise the seams
`proxyForward` / `containerForward` in their `TestMain`, so a developer's `HTTPS_PROXY` does not
change an exact argv. The `TestMain` of `internal/app`
also replaces `detectTools` (`internal/app/scan_tools.go`, production value `scan.Detect`) with an
empty report, so `App.Init` never runs the `trivy`, `gitleaks` and `plumber` of the machine
(DEVDESK-645); `TestInitDoesNotRunTheScannersOfTheHost` and `TestDetectToolsIsScanDetectInProduction`
guard it.

**Tests and the host secret store (DEVDESK-610).** By default `credentials.Select` and
`KeyringAvailable` reach the real keyring of the machine (Secret Service over D-Bus on
Linux); a locked keyring blocks the whole suite until the timeout. A test binary that can
reach them isolates the store: `fakekeyring.Install()` in `TestMain`, then
`fakekeyring.Fresh(t)` (or `FreshUnreachable(t, err)` for a locked keyring) per test, from
`internal/testutil/fakekeyring`. `isolateHome(t)` already calls `Fresh` in `internal/app` and
`internal/ui/setup`. Two guards enforce it: at run time, any keyring or `git credential` call
in a test binary without the fake panics with `DEVDESK-610` and the operation; statically,
`TestHostStoreGuard*` (`internal/credentials/hoststore_guard_test.go`) fails on K1 (go-keyring
imported outside `internal/credentials`), K2 (`SwapHostStoreForTest` in non-test code) and K3
(`fakekeyring` imported by non-test code). The seam is `credentials.HostStore` and
`SwapHostStoreForTest`, reserved for tests (it panics outside a test binary). Limits: the
runtime guard only sees the paths a test runs; the static one misses an aliased package
name, a dynamic import and an external binary; `gitHelperUsable` reads the git config
unguarded; `Install` and `Fresh` are global, so no `t.Parallel`. See
`docs/architecture/configuration.md`, "Testing code that reaches the secret store".

**Tests and real signals (DEVDESK-708, DEVDESK-711).** A test must never signal a real process. In
`internal/ports` the only place that does is `realOS.kill(pid, want, sig)` (`internal/ports/procos.go`),
reached through the `procOS` seam, which also holds `identity` and `probe` (`Probe` reads the state, it
sends no signal). `selfPID`, `parentPID`, `goos` and `now` are seams too. A test substitutes them
(`useFakeOS(t, self, parent, goos)` in `seams_test.go`); in `internal/ui/netdiag` it replaces `processOps`
on the model, so `ports.Kill`, `ports.Terminate` and `ports.Probe` are never reached.
`IdentityForTest` and `DeferredIdentityForTest` panic outside a test binary.
Two guards enforce it: at run time, a real signal in a test binary panics with `DEVDESK-708`
unless the test called `allowRealSignals(t)`, which only a test that kills a child it
started itself may do (`TestKillEndsARealChildProcess`, `TestTerminateEndsARealChildProcess` in
`stop_real_test.go`); statically, `TestOnlyRealOSSendsASignal`
fails on a signalling call (`os.FindProcess`, `syscall.Kill`, `unix.Kill`,
`windows.TerminateProcess`, `.Kill(` or `.Signal(`) outside `(realOS) kill`. Limits: the static
guard misses an aliased import, another package and an external binary; the seams are global, so
no `t.Parallel`. See `docs/architecture/network.md`, "Seams and the signal guard".

**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
literal `tea.KeyPressMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` returns a
`tea.KeyPressMsg` (`Keys` and `Type` return a message list), `Paste` a `tea.PasteMsg`; `Key` is strict: an unknown name
panics. The space key is built as a key (`Key("space")`), never matched through
`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). Lip Gloss v2 has no global colour profile (`Style.Render` always emits full
colour), so a test needs no setup to check styling; it reads the SGR or strips it
with `ansi.Strip`. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a
hand-built key, a `colorprofile` import outside `internal/app/profile_test.go` and
`internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go` or `SetColorProfile` in any `_test.go`. Paste tests
(`internal/app/paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input_test.go`, `component_form_test.go`):
a paste reaches the focused field, newlines become spaces in single-line fields,
and no key action fires (Rule 111).

**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as
`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Update
handlers switch on `tea.KeyPressMsg`, never the `tea.KeyMsg` interface (it also
matches releases). A paste is a `tea.PasteMsg`, not a key (Rule 111). Guards in
`internal/ui/keymap` (`space_scan_test.go`, `legacy_key_scan_test.go`,
`viewport_keymap_scan_test.go`) fail the suite otherwise; limits are listed in
`docs/architecture/app-shell.md`.

## Dependencies

Go 1.27 (`go 1.27.3` in `go.mod`). Key libraries (versions as in `go.mod`):
- `charm.land/bubbletea/v2` (v2.1.1) - TUI framework (v2: `tea.KeyPressMsg`, `tea.PasteMsg`, `View() tea.View`)
- `charm.land/bubbles/v2` (v2.2.1) - Pre-built TUI components (table, textinput, viewport)
- `charm.land/lipgloss/v2` (v2.0.6) - Styling (no global colour profile; colours are `image/color.Color`)
- `github.com/charmbracelet/colorprofile` (v0.4.3) - colour profile `main.go` forces under Windows Terminal (replaces `termenv`)
- `github.com/NimbleMarkets/ntcharts/v2` (v2.9.0) - dashboard sparkline
- `github.com/charmbracelet/x/ansi` - ANSI-safe width, strip and cut
- `gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go` - GitLab API client
- `github.com/prometheus-community/pro-bing` - ICMP ping functionality (maintained fork of go-ping/ping)
- `github.com/google/go-github/v68` - GitHub API client (§3.6)
- `github.com/libp2p/go-netroute` - which interface a destination leaves by, on all three platforms (§3.44)
- `golang.org/x/sys` - direct (Rule 303): the socket calls of `internal/nettrace` (`IP_TTL`, `IP_RECVERR`, `recvmsg` on the error queue); `x/sys/windows` serves `iphlpapi` (the Windows path trace, `IcmpSendEcho2`)
- `github.com/zalando/go-keyring` - host secret manager (wincred / Keychain / Secret Service), no cgo
- `gopkg.in/yaml.v3` - YAML configuration

## Code Conventions

- Comments: **English only** (Rule 307) — existing French comments are not rewritten wholesale, but any new or edited comment is in English
- Commit messages: **English only** (Rule 307)
- UI text and logs: **English US only** (Rule 129)
- Bubbletea models define their own message types
- Use `theme` package for consistent styling (`internal/ui/theme/`)
- Config changes must call `config.Save()` to persist
- All colors defined in `theme/colors.go`, all styles in `theme/styles.go`
- Message naming: `[ComponentName][Action]Msg` (e.g., `ComponentFormSubmitMsg`)
- Context names: the rule exists twice (`config.ValidateContextName`, `contextcmd.ValidName`); change both or neither (`TestContextNameRulesAgree`). Creation refuses `-`, `new`, `list` (`config.ValidateNewContextName`); loading does not (D91)

## Critical Bubble Tea Rules

**NEVER modify model state inside a Cmd** (Rule 110) - Race condition:
- `Update()` is the ONLY place to modify model state
- `View()` is read-only
- `Cmd` functions do I/O and return messages

**NEVER use `style.Render()` inside `table.Row{}`** (Rule 122) - ANSI sequences corrupt all subsequent rows:
- Use plain text: `theme.IconError + " error"` not `theme.StatusErrorStyle.Render(...)`
- Apply row styling via `table.SetStyles(theme.TableStylesForState("error"))`

**Views render through `Render()`** (Bubble Tea v2): a top-level view implements
`Render() string` and `View() tea.View { return tea.NewView(m.Render()) }`; only the
router (`App.View()`) sets terminal state such as `AltScreen` and `BackgroundColor`. Components keep
`View() string`. Colours are `color.Color`; hex literals stay in `theme/colors.go`.

**Update() case extraction**: If a case block exceeds 5 lines, extract to `handle[MessageType]()` method returning `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

</system-reminder>
